verdict: Pipeline is active, but overdue milestones are slowing your heating-season ramp.
narrative: In the last 28 days, paid tracking captured 7 leads at a cost of $232.05 each — a low volume number, though your CRM shows 264 contacts and 43 closed opportunities in the same window, meaning a meaningful share of activity is arriving through channels paid tracking alone doesn't fully count. Google Ads spend dropped 45% in the last 7 days against the prior 7, which has kept daily costs low ($60/day) but also kept volume near zero heading into heating season. The more pressing issue is operational: six agreed milestones are past due — most critically, the LSA heating toggles that were due September 1st and the intake owner confirmation that must be in place before budget can be scaled. Both are being resolved now, and the heating campaign launch target remains October 1st.

highlights.phrase: opportunities closed in the last 28 days per your CRM — well above what paid tracking alone shows
average daily ad spend this past week, pacing conservatively ahead of the heating-season ramp
actions taken on your Google Business profiles this period — calls, direction requests, and website clicks

watch_item.issue: LSA heating toggles are 13 days past their September 1st due date, and each day without them erodes the early heating-season demand window.
watch_item.fix: Re-enabling LSA heating campaigns is being prioritized this week to protect the October 1st full heating campaign launch date.
